title: Coarse graining on, all scale factors 1
purpose: Exercises the coarse-graining option of the `epsr` engine of EPSR [@soper1996,@soper2005], on when the first value of `qinscalefc` is > 1: per-molecule size factors `scalefacmol` (`.ato` molecule headers) and per-type sphere parameters `natomsph radminsph radmaxsph cgmolfac` define form factors and scale the reference-potential distances of molecule pairs [@epsrmanual]. This is the baseline case: coarse graining is on but every scale factor is 1.
system: The EPSR-test system: a liquid mixture of 200 dimethyl sulphoxide (DMSO, (CH3)2SO) and 400 water molecules (DMSO mole fraction 1/3; 3200 atoms) at 300 K in a cubic box of side 33.12 Å (atomic number density 0.0881 atoms/Å³). DMSO uses EPSR's Lennard-Jones + Coulomb reference potential with methyl rotational groups; water uses SPC/E Lennard-Jones and charge parameters [@berendsen1987] with EPSR's flexible intramolecular geometry (O-H 0.976 Å). The empirical potential is refined against three neutron diffraction data sets of deuterated DMSO in D2O, in null-scattering H2O/D2O and in H2O (ISIS SANDALS runs SLS03863, SLS03871, SLS03850), the isotope-substitution approach of Soper and Luzar [@soperluzar1992]. Coarse graining represents atoms by uniform spheres (form factors from `gaussianqr2` of the inner and outer radius); a molecule pair scales the reference-potential distance by `scalefac = 0.5*(scalefacmol(i)+scalefacmol(j))`. Here all `scalefacmol` = 1 and the atom types keep the defaults (`natomsph` 1, `radminsph` 0, `radmaxsph` = sigma/2, `cgmolfac` 1), giving one form-factor bin per type; H types have radius 0 and so density 0.
inputs: Generated from EPSR-test by `scripts/make_cg.py <folder> <mode>` (edits `.EPSR.inp` keywords, the `.ato` `scalefacmol` words and type columns). Mode for this case: `.EPSR.inp` `qinscalefc 2.0 0.0` (`selfbroadpwr` 0) and `ntimes 3`; `.ato` unchanged.
verification: The second pass reads back the `.ato` with its per-molecule scale factors and the `.EPSR.inp`, `.pcof`, `.inpa` and accumulators of the first. The coarse-graining block is active (log `inita> Average number of atoms per molecule: 2.00000000`), and the three list-directed files `formfactors.txt`, `intraformfactors.txt`, `intraformfactorsself.txt` are compared byte for byte in addition to the 27 standard outputs. With `scalefac` = 1 only these form-factor files differ from a run without coarse graining.
notes: Fortran: form factors and `wavinter` are computed but never used for S(Q) (the coarse-graining code in `gensq` is commented out).
